answer: At every oasis the water master counts the skins and chalks the tally on the lead camel's board, and no caravan may leave until the count balances. A juniper skin invented on the march fails the board: the quill of the count must match the skins hanging from the saddles, and an invented skin leaves men rationing dust. Faking the tally means running a caravan for a season, forging 180 oasis counts and paying 7,400, while the vault chalk on the board is checked by the caravan master at each halt, so water that was never carried is struck from the list.
